blocks.raw:
<Callout>
Megalithic architecture tests your understanding of the earliest monumental structures and the post-and-lintel system that dominated pre-classical building. The LEA expects you to identify key sites, construction methods, and the progression from simple dolmens to complex aligned stone arrangements.
</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory Aid: PPL System.** Post-and-lintel works because vertical posts support horizontal stones—think of it as stacking blocks vertically, then laying blocks horizontally on top. This simple principle repeated across centuries and cultures shows the power of fundamental engineering logic.
</Tip>

blocks.raw:
<Note>
**Key Clarification:** Megalithic does not mean monolithic. Megalithic = many large stones assembled together. Monolithic = a single carved stone (like an Egyptian obelisk). This distinction is testable and frequently confused.
</Note>

blocks.raw:
<Warn>
**Critical Distinction:** Do not overstate functional certainty. Many megalithic sites (stone circles, alignments) have proposed purposes—astronomical, ceremonial, territorial—but archaeological consensus is often lacking. Avoid asserting single functions for ambiguous structures like Stonehenge. Evidence suggests multiple purposes evolved over time.
</Warn>

blocks.raw: <Tip>**Megalithic vs. Monolithic:** Megalithic = many large stones assembled (Stonehenge). Monolithic = one single carved stone (Egyptian obelisk). This distinction is tested directly — do not confuse them.</Tip>
